summary: Typosquat of webpack's loader-utils ships obfuscated Function-constructor payload
details: Package `loader-utils-kit` impersonates webpack's `loader-utils`: `package.json` sets `author` to 'Tobias Koppers @sokra' and `repository.url` to `https://github.com/webpack/loader-utils.git`, and the README is copied from upstream. The tarball adds a file `lib/contract.js` not present in upstream `loader-utils`, which contains a seeded-permutation string decoder that reconstructs a code body and executes it through the `Function` constructor after assigning `require` and `module` onto `global`. The file is not referenced from the declared `main` (`lib/index.js`) and no lifecycle scripts are declared, so the payload does not fire on `npm install` or on `require('loader-utils-kit')` in this version — it activates only if a consumer explicitly requires `./contract`. The combination of identity-spoof metadata (author, repository URL, README) with an obfuscated Function-constructor payload shipped as a dormant trap is characteristic of a staged typosquat rather than a legitimate fork.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
